sovereign_country.strategic_role: 极速离岸证券与外汇交易商持牌（VFSC）、轻资产免税出海

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law and French Civil Law) - Unitary National Legal System
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transactions Reporting Act No. 62 of 2000, as amended; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Regulations made thereunder; International Companies Act [Cap. 222], ss. 10, 27 and 54 (confidential registers, registered agent obligations and name provisions); Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019; VFSC AML/CFT Supervisory Rules and Guidance Notes; Vanuatu Sanctions and United Nations Act [Cap. 147].

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport for each director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Vanuatu is a Contracting Party; if country of origin is not a Hague member, full Consular Legalization at the Vanuatu Mission or competent honorary consul applies)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin; alternative Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional and banking reference letter for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank, chartered accountant or licensed fiduciary of the applicant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / incumbency for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague registries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the VFSC-licensed Registered Agent and acceptance of appointment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the notary's competent authority; Consular Legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Curriculum vitae and business background statement for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant, countersigned by the notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, and the Vanuatu domestic sanctions list administered by the VFSC. Politically Exposed Persons, their family members and close associates are automatically classified as higher-risk and require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and senior management sign-off in accordance with Financial Transactions Reporting Act s. 42 and VFSC guidance. Screening is re-run on a rolling 90-day cycle throughout the client relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Companies Online Registration Portal; name clearance and reservation are submitted exclusively through a VFSC-licensed Registered Agent under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222].
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be expressed in English or French (or any language using the Latin alphabet) and must end with a limited liability designator: 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporated', 'Inc.', 'Corporation', 'Corp.' or 'Société Anonyme'. No mandatory local-script or Bislama transliteration is required; however, if a Bislama word is used the Registrar may request an English or French translation to confirm that the name is not undesirable or misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Vanuatu', 'Republic', 'Government', 'National', 'President', 'State', 'Authority' (token requires prior ministerial approval as it suggests a connection with the Government of Vanuatu)

'Bank', 'Trust', 'Fiduciary', 'Insurance', 'Reinsurance', 'Assurance' (triggers licensing under the Banking Act, Insurance Act or fiduciary licensing regime and is generally prohibited for a standard IC)
'Financial Services', 'Broker', 'Fund', 'Investment', 'Superannuation', 'Securities', 'Exchange' (sensitive tokens requiring VFSC regulatory approval and an appropriate licence)
'University', 'Chamber of Commerce', 'Cooperative', 'Building Society' (statutorily reserved and prohibited without the consent of the relevant authority)

Any name that is identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered company, or that the Registrar considers 'undesirable', contrary to public policy, or suggestive of a criminal purpose under ICA Cap. 222, s. 10
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: the licensed Registered Agent must file a written extension application with the VFSC before the expiry of the initial reservation; each approved extension renews the reservation for another 30 days, with a maximum cumulative reservation period of 90 days and a fixed extension fee. Rejection appeal: the proposed incorporator files a written reconsideration request through the Registered Agent within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, setting out the grounds; the VFSC Registrar must issue a decision within 14 days. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an originating application for judicial review in the Supreme Court of Vanuatu. In parallel, the applicant may immediately refile under a different, distinguishable name without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. The statutory registered office must be the physical address of the VFSC-licensed Registered Agent in Port Vila, which serves as the IC's service address; day-to-day management, bookkeeping and the entire online cosmetics DTC retail operation may be conducted remotely from outside Vanuatu with no in-territory employee or physical premises. If the IC is subsequently deemed tax resident in Vanuatu and conducts a 'distribution and service centre' relevant activity, the Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2019 requires economic substance in the form of local board meetings, local employees and proportionate local expenditure; for a non-resident, tax-exempt offshore IC with no Vanuatu-source income, no substance obligation attaches.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - approximately 10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk, unlicensed, non-resident International Company with a compliant Registered Agent. The probability escalates to approximately 45% if the economic substance notification or annual return is overdue, if the Registered Agent fails CDD refresh, or if sanctions/PEP screening flags arise during the VFSC supervisory cycle.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act [Cap 222] (Vanuatu), as amended, ss 4-11 (incorporation), s 12 (prohibited domestic business), ss 33-36 (registered office and registered agent), ss 37-40 (directors and secretary)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) – Registry of International Companies, Port Vila
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; shares may be issued for such consideration as the board determines, and the Registrar performs no paid-up capital verification at incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company shall issue one thousand ordinary shares at par value to the initial subscriber set forth in the register of members, and that the Secretary be and is hereby directed to record such allotment in the share register. RESOLVED that the Company do adopt the registered office of the licensed registered agent at the address filed with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, and that the Registered Agent be retained under the standard agency agreement. RESOLVED that the offices of Director and Secretary are hereby established, and the persons named in the incumbency certificate are appointed as first Director and first Secretary, each to hold office until removed in accordance with the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC, Registry of International Companies (counter and online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request in English listing the proposed corporate name, ISIC 4791 activity description (online retail of cosmetics and personal care), and the intended first director and secretary. Verify against the VFSC database for prohibited, identical, or confusingly similar names and restricted words. Obtain the written name clearance certificate before filing.
required_dossiers: Photographic ID and address proof of incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as similar or restricted, file an amended request with a distinctive alternative name within 14 days; first re-submission attracts no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed VFSC registered agent (law firm or corporate services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a VFSC-licensed agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in compliance with the International Companies Act, including authorised share capital, director indemnity clauses, and objects covering online cosmetics retail, e-commerce logistics, and ancillary ancillary trading. Execute the charter and have the agent countersign as sponsor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any clause, the agent re-drafts the affected provision and re-submits with a covering response; corrections are typically cured within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application to VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 together with the executed charter, name clearance certificate, agent consent, and director declaration. The Registrar performs completeness and legality review, and upon approval issues a registration entry and certificate.
required_dossiers: Consent to act of registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VFSC issues a request for further information, respond with the requested particulars within 14 calendar days; failure to respond renders the application deemed withdrawn with fees refunded less processing costs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of incorporation and annual registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Finance Office / VFSC online payment gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the USD 300 incorporation fee plus the first annual registration fee in US dollars or Vatu equivalent by wire transfer or other VFSC-approved method. Retain the payment receipt referencing the VFSC application number.
required_dossiers: VFSC invoice or application reference number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is rejected, verify the VFSC bank codes and re-remit; accidental overpayment is credited against the following year's annual fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful review and fee confirmation, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the seal of the Commission. The company is constituted as a body corporate with limited liability on the date stated in the certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, submit a written rectification request to the Registrar; administrative correction is completed within 5 business days at no charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting by written resolution or unanimous consent to adopt the registered office, approve share subscription, appoint officers, and authorise bank account opening. Establish the register of members, register of directors and secretaries, incumbency certificate, and corporate minute book at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a counterparty or bank queries incumbency, order a certificate of incumbency from VFSC and certified charter extracts; any register inconsistencies must be cured by board resolution and updated filings within 5 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – International Companies are statutorily prohibited from carrying on domestic business in Vanuatu under s 12 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222], and are therefore outside the scope of the Business Licence Act [Cap 247] local licensing regime
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Nil – no local operating, manufacturing, or retail premises permit is required for an offshore-facing online cosmetics retail business; product import and safety registrations in destination consumer markets may apply separately

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology and Geo-Hazards, Vanuatu
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – full EIA Report not triggered by a virtual or light-asset e-commerce operation; if a third-party distribution warehouse is later established, a low-impact Registration (Category 3) may be required under the Vanuatu Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or point-source VOC emissions are authorised or generated by online retail activity; packaging waste and expired cosmetic products must be handled through licensed waste carriers under the Vanuatu Waste Management Act; flammable aerosol inventory, if any, must not exceed the storage thresholds requiring special environmental registration

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for virtual-only operations; if a physical warehouse or office is established, obtain fire safety certification from the Vanuatu Fire and Emergency Service, a structural load inspection of racking and mezzanines by a registered engineer, and an occupational health and safety clearance from the Vanuatu Department of Labour covering stock handling hygiene and staff welfare

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Department of Customs and Inland Revenue (DCIR), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, Government of Vanuatu - VAT and customs administration is exercised through the Commissioner of Inland Revenue and the Director of Customs; International Company registration is administered by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC). Official e-services portal: www.gov.vu (VAT, customs ASYCUDA World, and business license procedures); VFSC portal: www.vfsc.vu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporation: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) is incorporated under the International Companies Act [Cap. 212] through a VFSC-licensed registered agent; the VFSC company number and certificate of incorporation are the statutory corporate identifiers. Step 2 - No income-tax TIN: Vanuatu levies no corporate income tax and issues no general TIN; no national tax registration is required for an offshore IC whose business is conducted outside Vanuatu. Step 3 - VAT ID for onshore supplies: an IC making taxable supplies in Vanuatu must apply to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue for VAT registration on the prescribed form, attaching the certificate of incorporation, registered agent and registered office details, bank account information, and projected turnover; the issued VAT registration number is the only tax identifier. Step 4 - Business license: any onshore business activity requires a municipal business license (Port Vila, Luganville, or other municipality) or a license issued through the DCIR outside municipal boundaries. Step 5 - Annual maintenance: the IC must maintain a licensed registered agent in Vanuatu and pay VFSC annual fees to preserve its exempt status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - A Vanuatu International Company is statutorily exempt from all Vanuatu taxes, duties, levies, and imposts on offshore income, profits, distributions, and capital gains; Vanuatu has no corporate income tax, no withholding tax, and no capital gains tax for any taxpayer. Onshore taxable supplies remain subject to the 12.5% VAT and municipal business license fees, but no entity-level profits tax is imposed. Pass_Through_Eligible is not separately recognized because Vanuatu has no income tax to pass through.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic check-the-box, hybrid-mismatch, CFC, thin-capitalization, or entity-classification election exists because Vanuatu imposes no income tax. The relevant statutory elections are: (i) voluntary VAT registration for taxable persons below the VT 10,000,000 compulsory turnover threshold; (ii) selection of the VAT filing cycle (monthly or quarterly) as prescribed by the Commissioner, with a concessional VT 5,000,000 threshold available to tourism-related operators; and (iii) a VFSC-filed election to convert an IC to, or from, a local company, which changes the tax-exempt characterization. The offshore tax exemption itself is automatic and requires no election or filing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - a destination-based consumption tax administered under the Value Added Tax Act No. 6 of 1998 (as amended); Vanuatu does not operate a separate GST, sales tax, or use tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 10,000,000 (ten million vatu) of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; a lower VT 5,000,000 sectoral threshold applies to tourism-related operators; voluntary registration is permitted below the compulsory threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None - Vanuatu does not mandate e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, government API reporting, or digital stamping. Taxpayers may issue paper or PDF VAT invoices with the prescribed particulars. Customs export formalities are submitted electronically through the ASYCUDA World system and the Vanuatu Trade Portal; no real-time tax-authority invoice clearance applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) applies under the Value Added Tax Act No. 6 of 1998 (as amended) to: (a) goods physically exported from Vanuatu by the supplier, including cross-border DTC consignments of cosmetics delivered to overseas consumers; (b) services supplied to a non-resident located outside Vanuatu at the time of supply, excluding services connected with Vanuatu land or goods; and (c) international transport and related freight and insurance. The supplier must be the exporter of record and must maintain contemporaneous documentary evidence of physical export, sale value, and receipt of consideration in convertible currency. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated supplies is creditable, and any excess credit is refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Validated Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World export declaration) showing the cosmetics consignment, HS classification, FOB value, and final destination outside Vanuatu.
Bill of lading, airway bill, or carrier-endorsed courier/sea-freight receipt evidencing physical removal of the goods from Vanuatu.

Commercial invoice and export packing list referencing the export declaration and evidencing the overseas buyer and 0% VAT treatment, together with banking evidence of receipt of export proceeds (inward remittance certificate or foreign-currency bank statement).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Vanuatu has no foreign-exchange control law, so no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline exists and no clawback is triggered by timing of repatriation. However, the Commissioner of Inland Revenue may audit zero-rating claims within the assessment periods of the VAT Act 1998 and, where export substantiation is false, deficient, or fraudulent, may: (i) issue a default assessment charging VAT at 12.5% on the full sales value; (ii) impose late-payment interest and civil penalties at the statutory rates; (iii) pursue criminal sanctions for fraudulent evasion against the IC and its officers, including fines and imprisonment for natural persons; and (iv) retrospectively claw back the zero-rating benefit, input VAT credits, and refunds previously paid.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu operates under a broadly liberalised, non-restrictive exchange-control framework. There are no legally imposed exchange controls on current-account transactions, capital transfers, or profit remittances by International Companies. The VUV is convertible in practice, subject to the commercial anti-money-laundering checks of the banking institution executing the transfer. Profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders is generally permitted without central bank prior approval, provided that the bank receives the supporting audited financial statements, board resolution, and tax-clearance or confirmation of the entity's tax-exempt status where requested. The primary hurdles are not statutory but documentary: source-of-funds verification, beneficial-ownership disclosure, and correspondent-bank due diligence on VUV-to-USD transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vanuatu imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. A licensed cosmetic-beauty retailer may receive export proceeds directly into its offshore-capable VUV or multi-currency account and may retain, convert, or disburse such proceeds freely. The only reporting obligation arises under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act and the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, under which international wire transfers above the applicable threshold require transaction reporting to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit. Banks may request supporting invoices and customs declarations for compliance verification but do not require conversion of foreign currency into VUV.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-to-Medium for offshore digital EMI services. Vanuatu's regulatory environment does not currently provide a dedicated local electronic-money-institution licence, and the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission is not a passporting member of the EU/UK EMI regimes. An offshore digital EMI may serve the e-commerce treasury structure only if the EMI relies on a correspondent banking partner in Vanuatu, Australia, or New Zealand and obtains an appropriate payable-through or settlement arrangement. Legal constraints include: the absence of a local EMI licence framework, onboarding requirements for a Vanuatu International Company under the AML/CFT rules, and the heightened risk of account restriction due to the perceived use of digital-only financial institutions. EmiS without tier-1 correspondent banking relationships are not viable as the primary settlement rail.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Vanuatu banks generally require physical presence for at least one director or the designated company secretary/agent signatory at account opening when the entity is non-resident-owned. Remote opening is available only through an approved Vanuatu-licensed registered agent who certifies all identity documents and performs in-person verification; video-conference interview is conditionally accepted by some banks provided the client appears before a notarising officer and original identity documents are presented. A physical or agency-signed KYC interview is therefore effectively mandatory. Corporate signatories must provide the original or certified bank-signing resolution, copy of the Certificate of Incorporation, copies of the Register of Directors and Members, a recent utility bill or banker's reference for each director, and an authenticated proof of business activity such as the e-commerce platform seller contract and brand licence agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vanuatu International Company classified as a tax-exempt offshore structure with no taxable presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and International Company Certificate, current Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, board resolution confirming business purpose, notarized passport copies of all directors/beneficial owners, recent utility bills, and a signed economic-substance attestation that management and control activities are conducted through a licensed registered agent in Vanuatu.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and remote management with no clear commercial nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly notarised board minutes authorising the Vanuatu-registered agent to manage bank communications, executed registered-agent agreement, certified copy of the e-commerce retail platform seller agreement, supplier purchase orders, customs/trade documents, and a written explanation of the physical flow of goods proving that the Vanuatu IC is a genuine distribution and payment intermediary rather than a shell treasury vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity injections from unrelated shareholders exceeding reporting thresholds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription agreement, audited or accountant-certified financial statements of the injecting shareholder, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, securities sale contract, dividend warrant), corporate authorisation from the injecting company, and a transaction purpose declaration referencing the ISIC 4791 cosmetics retail expansion plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to global FinTech PSPs such as Shopify Payments and PayPal triggering high-risk merchant flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier commercial invoices and pro-forma contracts, end-customer order records and refund policy evidence, product registration/certification documents (e.g. GMP and safety data sheets for cosmetics), trademark and brand licence agreements, and a comprehensive AML transaction-flow diagram showing from-beneficiary-to-payee settlement mechanics.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VFSC Annual Return confirming registered particulars, members and directors (International Companies Act annual filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation: annual return and government renewal fee due on the anniversary and must be lodged within one month after that date; agents may request a short grace period at the sole discretion of VFSC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: US$100 late filing penalty; if the annual return and fee remain outstanding for more than 60 days after the anniversary, VFSC may strike the company off the International Companies Register and the company ceases to be an exempt entity for that continued period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation and UBO Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual return; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership during the year must be reported to VFSC within 30 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VFSC infringement notice of approximately VUV 25,000 (about US$210) per non-notified change; persistent failure may disqualify directors and prevent the registered agent from issuing the company's certificate of good standing, and may trigger compulsory strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent Renewal Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent under the International Companies Act, on behalf of VFSC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously maintained throughout the year; any change of registered agent or registered office must be filed with VFSC within 7 days of the change, with formal re-confirmation at each annual anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a Vanuatu-registered agent and registered office automatically suspends the company's legal transaction capacity and is an immediate trigger for administrative deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit for a Vanuatu International Company: no revenue, asset or size threshold triggers an audit for a non-licensed IC. Compulsory audit applies only to VFSC-licensed activities such as banking, insurance, securities dealing, and trust or company service providers, or where the company's constitution or a regulatory licence imposes an audit condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) for any voluntarily prepared or licence-required audited financial statements; Vanuatu does not maintain a domestic GAAP regime for International Companies, and non-licensed ICs are not required to file accounts with VFSC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Vanuatu International Company must maintain an internal beneficial ownership register and file an annual UBO confirmation with VFSC at the same time as its annual return. Share transfers must be recorded and any resulting change in beneficial ownership reported within 30 days; the company is not permitted to pay dividends or make distributions to a new transferee until the register has been updated and the annual UBO confirmation reflects the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute; voluntary certified audit US$2,500 – US$6,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective corporate income tax rate; International Companies under the International Companies Act [Cap.222] are exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, distribution tax, and stamp duties. There are no statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions because the base CIT liability is zero. The only recurring charges are the VFSC annual registration fee (up to VUV 55,000 depending on authorised capital) and, where local sales are made, value-added tax at 15%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Vanuatu corporate income tax return exists. The only periodic filing is the International Company Annual Return and Annual Fee submitted by a VFSC-licensed registered agent through the VFSC e-Registry portal. Form identifier: VFSC-IC Annual Return/Annual Renewal (no tax return code is assigned).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return must be delivered to the registered agent within 2 months after the anniversary of incorporation. The VFSC annual fee is separately payable by the invoice due date shown on the VFSC renewal notice, normally 30 June of each calendar year for standard files.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company and VFSC company registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact registered English name; no Vanuatu taxpayer identification number is required because the entity is tax-exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office in Vanuatu and details of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent's physical address must be stated; a non-resident owner may not use a PO Box for the registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised share capital, issued shares, class of shares, and currency of share capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of shares; no minimum paid-up capital is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full name, residential address, nationality, and identification details of each director.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are permitted; no local director or alternate director is required for an International Company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beneficial ownership schedule including ultimate individual owners and controllers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each non-resident beneficial owner must submit the VFSC beneficial ownership declaration, together with passport and proof of address, through the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax exemption declaration confirming that the entity continues to qualify as an International Company under the International Companies Act [Cap.222] and is not carrying on a licensed or prescribed activity in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident owner should confirm in writing that no Vanuatu-source trading income is being generated and that no tax return is required; this supports the zero-tax filing position.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission of the Annual Return and non-payment of the annual fee trigger a fixed late penalty (typically 20% of the annual fee) plus daily surcharges of VUV 500 per day after the due date. Persistent default for three months may result in automatic VFSC strike-off. Knowingly filing a false annual return is an offence under s.158 of the International Companies Act, punishable by a fine of up to VUV 1,000,000 and imprisonment; directors may also be disqualified from acting as directors in Vanuatu.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (no dividend withholding tax is levied by Vanuatu).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has not entered into a comprehensive double tax agreement and imposes no withholding tax on outbound dividends. Consequently, there is no treaty-relief filing mechanism and no Vanuatu tax-residence certificate can reduce a withholding tax obligation because no such tax is chargeable. If a non-resident shareholder requires formal proof of the entity's status, the company may apply to the VFSC for a Certificate of Status; that certificate is administrative evidence of registration and does not confer any tax treaty benefit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding tax on royalty and interest payments made to non-residents. No treaty reduction is required because Vanuatu imposes no source withholding tax on IP royalties or debt interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 0 VUV (no domestic transfer pricing statute and no Local File/Master File obligation in Vanuatu). Because Vanuatu has no corporate income tax, the IC has no Vanuatu transfer-pricing compliance duty. However, if the ultimate parent or beneficial owner is tax-resident in a jurisdiction with transfer pricing rules, related-party cross-border transactions of the IC may be subject to that foreign jurisdiction's documentation thresholds, e.g. EUR 750,000 or the equivalent local currency threshold for intercompany services, royalties, and financing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu does not currently impose a domestic Economic Substance Return on a non-licensed International Company engaged in online retail. The online sale of cosmetics and personal care products is not a prescribed activity requiring a Vanuatu financial Services licence. ESR-style substance obligations may be triggered only if the IC is managed and controlled in Vanuatu and conducts a regulated financial activity, or if a foreign jurisdiction applies OECD/EU substance requirements to the IC for CFC/treaty purposes. For a pure e-commerce structure, the commercial substance (inventory, employees, logistics, and management decisions) should sit in the operating jurisdiction in which sales are made or in the parent's residence to avoid a sham/shell finding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / deliberate suppression of taxable profit in the operating country
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the tax-exempt Vanuatu IC as the invoicing entity while the actual sales, inventory, personnel, and management of the cosmetics business are located in a high-tax jurisdiction, thereby concealing a permanent establishment and understating taxable profit in that jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The operating jurisdiction may assess the full profit on the basis that the Vanuatu IC is a sham, together with interest at statutory rates and penalties of 20% to 100% of the tax understated. In Vanuatu, filing a false declaration with the VFSC is an offence under s.158 of the International Companies Act, subject to a fine up to VUV 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign misleading invoices or tax declarations may be made personally liable for civil restitution of unpaid foreign taxes. Foreign criminal courts may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and custodial sentences of up to seven years for tax evasion, and the corporate veil will be pierced where fraud or sham conduct is shown.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Vanuatu IC with no employees, no premises, no bank account in the company's name, and no commercial substance while claiming zero-tax status for real e-commerce operations and interposing the IC purely to avoid foreign tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu may strike off the IC for failing to maintain a registered agent and annual fee compliance. In foreign jurisdictions, anti-avoidance rules can re-attribute the IC's revenue and assets to the beneficial owner, impose CFC taxation, and levy penalties of up to 25% of the tax adjustment. Where a licence or ESR regime applies, fines may be substantial and the IC can be struck off.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil if the IC is a mere facade; directors may be jointly and severally liable for the foreign tax liabilities and may be prohibited from managing companies for up to 15 years. Serious cases may lead to extradition, asset restraining orders, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CFT compliance failure / unauthorised payment processing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payment card proceeds through Shopify Payments and PayPal without conducting customer due diligence, without identifying beneficial owners of corporate customers, and without maintaining an anti-money-laundering compliance programme required for payment intermediaries or reporting entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Vanuatu Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act [Cap.249], breaches can result in fines up to VUV 20,000,000, forfeiture of transaction proceeds, and suspension of the registered agent. The VFSC may also strike off the company for failure to maintain a lawful registered agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly facilitate money laundering face criminal liability, imprisonment of up to fifteen years, asset confiscation, travel bans, and personal disqualification orders. The corporate veil is pierced for AML offences, and beneficial owners may be named in public enforcement actions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive tax-residence certificate and false treaty representation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a VFSC Certificate of Status or Certificate of Residence to represent to banks or tax authorities that the Vanuatu IC is resident in a country with a double-tax treaty, or that interest, royalty, or dividend payments are exempt from withholding due to a non-existent Vanuatu treaty benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Misuse of a residence certificate is treated as fraudulent misrepresentation in the recipient jurisdiction and as an offence in Vanuatu under s.158 of the International Companies Act. The certificate may be revoked retroactively, the entity struck off, and fines imposed in both the foreign jurisdiction and Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly furnish false certificates may be subject to personal restitution obligations, criminal fines, imprisonment, and Interpol red notices where the misrepresentation is used to move funds across borders. Foreign tax authorities may issue a travel ban pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-arm's-length transfer pricing and margin stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Causing the Vanuatu IC to purchase cosmetics from a related manufacturer at inflated prices, to pay excessive royalties to a related brand owner, or to earn no economic margin, thereby shifting profit away from the foreign operating company into the zero-tax Vanuatu entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Although Vanuatu has no TP law, the foreign parent's tax authority can make transfer-pricing adjustments, disallow deductions, impose interest rates of 3% to 5% per annum, and apply penalties of 20% to 40% of the adjusted amount. Aggressive related-party arrangements may also trigger general anti-avoidance and fraud penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers approving false transfer-pricing documentation may incur personal liability for the taxpayer's penalty and interest where they signed declarations or caused the understatement. Courts may pierce the veil, impose civil restitution, issue travel bans, and refer directors for criminal prosecution in serious fraud cases.
